rule: Plant Protection and Quarantine Proclamation 1400/2026 is the current starting point, replacing reliance on the 1992 law. Processed products are covered where pest risk remains, and article 4 provides import controls; a current list resolving finished tea was not located.
personalMailApplicability: No personal postal tea exemption established under the new law.
remainingQuestion: The finished-tea pest-risk classification under Plant Protection and Quarantine Proclamation 1400/2026 remains missing. Separately, establish how Proclamation 1112/2019 article 3 and any current EFDA food directive apply to an own-consumption postal purchase. The recovered 2014 directive expressly exempts personal food from competence licensing, but does not establish a current waiver from shipment certificates; its company-trade scope also prevents treating article 20 as an unqualified private import duty.
researchAttempts: Located and read the new 2026 proclamation rather than carrying forward the superseded law; searched commodity schedules and personal-use exceptions.

Reconfirmed on 30 September 2026 that the Ministry of Justice lists Proclamation 1400/2026 as in force from 7 May 2026. Re-attempted the official PDF and searched current commodity schedules and exact-title mirrors; official PDF retrieval returned 403 in this follow-up. No new tea-specific implementing classification or private-post exception was established, so the earlier unresolved finding is preserved rather than falling back to the repealed 1992 law.

30 September independent food/conformity pass: Recovered actual Gazette Proclamation 1112/2019 and visually verified article 10(1), PDF page 20: food imports require safety compliance and an executive-organ permit. However article 3, PDF page 13, limits the law’s scope to products intended for market placement or otherwise offered for public use. Article2(1) defines food to include processed human-consumption substances. Regulation 531/2023 defines the agency and its powers, not a new unqualified private import duty. The current eRIS portal describes special import applications but in an importer/vendor/licensing chain; it does not settle private personal food parcels. Complete FAO-hosted Gazette law and 2023 agency regulation downloaded; article 10 visually verified because PDF OCR is poor. Ministry of Justice labels 1112/2019 in force. Personal medical/supplement exceptions and customs tax allowances were not extended to ordinary tea.

30 September legal-scope peer review: recovered the complete official English translation of Food Exporters, Importers and Wholesalers Control Directive 22/2014, hosted by USDA. Article 4 limits it to food-trade companies; article 8(1) expressly exempts personal-consumption food from the certificate of competence. Article 20(4) separately lists shipment health and origin certificates, and article 8 does not expressly waive those. This is an older directive and its present interaction with Proclamation 1112/2019 was not established. The 2025 USDA FAIRS report describes processed tea notification and commercial import documents but supplies no private-postal scope rule; its reliance on the 1992 plant regulation cannot override the new 2026 proclamation. These sources narrow the licensing issue without clearing tea or proving an unavoidable private-parcel certificate.
